subject: Veridian: incident RCA readout and executive commitments
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Sara Patel <sara.p@veridian.com>
Date: 2027-12-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Incident 2027-12-06 — preliminary findings and timeline

Marissa / Hannah —

Quick summary of what the on-call team found in the first 24 hours:

1) Trigger: a rolling kernel upgrade on a small subset of our serving fleet that coincided with a spike in long-tail sequence lengths from Veridian’s batch workload. The upgrade introduced a subtle change in CUDA memory allocation behavior for the affected kernel path.

2) Failure mode: under a specific seq-len distribution the runtime attempted to allocate and then evict KV cache pages more aggressively; combined with a race in the autoscaling controller this caused transient OOMs and token-drop errors for sessions pinned to those hosts.

3) Scope: ~3% of Veridian requests (peak window 2027-12-06T02:04–02:43Z), higher error rate on long chat sessions. We contained impact by removing the new kernel and routing Veridian traffic off the affected host pool by 02:52Z.

Immediate remediation completed: kernel roll-back, hotfix to controller backoff, and temporary routing rule to enforce session affinity to healthy pools.

We need to produce a short, customer-friendly RCA and a concrete implementation plan that includes: exact timeline, root cause explanation (non-technical summary + technical appendix), action owners with deadlines, and verification steps. I’ll assemble the draft but wanted alignment on exec asks and any compensation language — Sean, can you propose the commercial remediation options?

-David

--
David Kim
Head of Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.p@veridian.com>, Tom Brooks <tom.b@veridian.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-09T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Veridian — RCA summary and next steps (attached)

Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for your patience while we completed the technical review. Attached is a concise RCA summary and an implementation plan with owners and timelines. Below is the customer-facing summary; the attachment (veridian_rca_summary.pdf) contains the technical appendix and annotated timeline.

Executive summary (for your stakeholders):
- What happened: A recently deployed kernel optimization on a small subset of our GPU fleet interacted with Veridian’s traffic profile (long-session requests and variable sequence lengths). That interaction caused intermittent KV-cache eviction and memory allocation thrashing for a narrow host pool, which led to degraded request success rates for a subset of your sessions during the 2027-12-06 incident window.
- Impact: Approx. 3% of your requests during the peak ~40-minute window experienced token-drop or transient failures. There was no data exfiltration and no change to stored customer data.
- Containment and mitigation: We rolled back the kernel change within 40 minutes, added a temporary routing policy to avoid the affected pool, and deployed a controller backoff fix.

Planned corrective actions (high level) — full details in attached spreadsheet:
1) Kernel hardening and additional preflight tests (owner: Reliability, lead: David Kim) — completion target: 2028-01-10
2) Controller race fix & improved autoscaler telemetry (owner: Platform, lead: Hannah Schmitt) — completion target: 2027-12-22
3) Traffic-shaping rule improvements and session affinity guardrails for long sessions (owner: Serving, lead: Marissa Cole) — completion target: 2027-12-29
4) Customer verification window + smoke tests with Veridian (joint runbook; owner: Customer Success, lead: Sean Gallagher) — verification window: 2028-01-03 to 2028-01-05

Commercial remediation: Sean has suggested a one-time service credit to offset the affected usage in December; Sean — I’ve put a suggested credit range in the attached timeline spreadsheet for your review and will follow with a formal credit memo once you confirm.

Immediate asks from Veridian: please confirm if your security/compliance team would like the technical appendix redacted before wider distribution, and confirm a preferred time for a 30-minute readout next week (proposed: 2027-12-13 10:00–10:30 PT).

Attachments: veridian_rca_summary.pdf (RCA + technical appendix), veridian_implementation_timeline.xlsx (action owners & dates)

Best,
Marissa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Patel <sara.p@veridian.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Brooks <tom.b@veridian.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-10T08:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Veridian — RCA summary and next steps (attached)

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear summary and the fast turnaround. A couple quick items from our side:

1) Our SOC/compliance team will want the full technical appendix for their review; please include any relevant logs, SHA hashes of the kernel binaries, and the test matrix you used to validate the rollback. We can sign an NDA addendum if needed.
2) The verification window dates look fine; please treat the test runs as production-paced so we validate under load.
3) Regarding credits: we need a concrete % calculation tied to the impacted token volume for Dec 6 — if you can provide the token counts and your proposed calculation we’ll route the proposed credit to procurement.

For the readout, 2027-12-13 10:00 PT works for Tom and me. Please send a calendar invite and the final summary beforehand.

Thanks —
Sara
VP, Platform Engineering
Veridian Financial
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.p@veridian.com>, Tom Brooks <tom.b@veridian.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-11T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Veridian — RCA summary and next steps (attached)

Sara / Tom —

Thanks — confirmed for 2027-12-13 10:00 PT (calendar invite sent). A few concrete follow-ups from our side ahead of the readout:

A) Deliverables we will provide before the readout (by 2027-12-12 15:00 PT):
   - Final customer-facing RCA PDF (veridian_rca_summary.pdf) — with an unredacted technical appendix sent under an NDA addendum if you confirm.
   - Exact impacted token counts and the credit calculation spreadsheet (CSV + summary tab).
   - Runbook excerpt showing the temporary routing and rollback steps we executed.

B) Action owner checklist (quick view):
   - David Kim: kernel hardening plan + preflight test matrix (target 2028-01-10)
   - Hannah Schmitt: controller race fix + telemetry rollout (target 2027-12-22)
   - Marissa Cole: session-affinity guardrails + traffic-shaping release (target 2027-12-29)
   - Sean Gallagher: proposed credit memo and procurement-facing wording (target 2027-12-12)

C) Verification plan: joint smoke tests during 2028-01-03 — we’ll co-ordinate a 2-hour production-paced window and share an acceptance checklist.

We’re tracking the implementation tasks in OPS-4886; I’ll attach a read-only Drive folder and the timeline spreadsheet to the calendar invite so your procurement and compliance teams can access materials before the call.

If you’d like an expanded executive note for your board or risk committee, we can provide a 1-page summary with the impact, mitigations, and our commitment timeline.

Appreciate your partnership.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments referenced: veridian_rca_summary.pdf (attached to thread), veridian_implementation_timeline.xlsx (attached to thread)
